text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Observability pipeline detected sustained sampling/drop anomalies for Datadog host metrics and traces in us-east-1. Several dashboards reporting data gaps and alerts queued. auto-severity: P2. React with :eyes: if you're taking ownership.
Sam: seeing blank heatmaps on the request-rate dashboard, traces missing for a ton of services. Alerts are piling but the alert delivery itself looks delayed.
Elaine: I'm oncall for infra, taking lead. tagging @Tara for customer-impact.
Tara: noticed a couple of customer support tickets about missing traces for signup flows — looks like metric spikes are present in internal Prometheus but Datadog graphs are stale.
Mike: confirming — host-level metrics are delayed ~10-15m and trace sampling rate is inconsistent. App logs still arrive to S3 so we can fallback to raw logs if needed.
Nora: filing an incident ticket now: RED-INC-2026-341. Adding initial impact: partial telemetry loss in us-east-1 (metrics+traces).
Josh: pinging Datadog support and posting to status: https://status.datadoghq.com — customer reported an ingest backlog earlier.
datadog-status-bot: UPDATE from Datadog: "Investigating — ingestion backlog causing sampling and dashboard delays in us-east-1. Engineers are looking into queueing layer." (link: https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/abcd1234)
Elaine: quick triage: is this causing SLO breaches or user-facing errors? we need to know before paging on-call pagerduty.
Sam: app metrics show increased 5xx for payments in a subset of hosts. Not sure if real or artifact because traces missing. Cross-checking with CloudWatch now.
Tara: Customer impact quick note: Billing ingestion and fraud-detection pipelines depend on timely traces. If this persists >30m we should notify enterprise customers (AcmeCorp, BlueCart).
Mike: mitigation plan: 1) switch critical alerts to fallback signal (Prometheus/CloudWatch) 2) enable verbose logging for payments services 3) queue a temporary sampling override to capture more traces locally (we'll store to S3 for post-hoc analysis).
Nora: logging runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/observability-fallback (adding to incident ticket).
Elaine: Sam/Tara/Mike do the switch. I'll coordinate with support to draft a customer status note.
Sam: executed alert flip: ran: ```# temporary alert source change
for alert in $(cat critical-alerts.txt); do frontend_cli alert set-source --id $alert --source prometheus; done
``` :white_check_mark: Alerts now firing from prometheus for the critical set.
Mike: enabling verbose logs: pushed a small flag to prod (LOG_SAMPLING=full) via k8s rollout on payments deployment. watchers: expect increased logging and storage.
Tara: sending initial customer advisory (internal draft): "We're seeing delayed telemetry ingestion to Datadog in us-east-1 which may affect traces and dashboards. We're actively mitigating by switching critical alerting to alternate telemetry sources and will update within 30 minutes." Will post to status page after Elaine review.
Sam: I also opened a short-lived local trace buffer: `dd-local-bufferer` writing raw spans to s3://redwood-incident-backups/2352109876/ — capture started.
Josh: Datadog support responded: "We're throttling ingestion to stabilize queues. ETA for normalization unknown. We'll update every 15 minutes." Also provided a debug token to share with our agent team.
Elaine: good. action items: - keep alerts on fallback - continue capturing raw traces - prepare PSR (post-incident summary) - escalate to platform eng if sampling anomalies persist 30m+
Nora: noted. adding assignees: Sam (alerts), Mike (logs/traces buffer), Josh (Datadog liaison), Tara (customer comms), Elaine (incident lead).
Sam: quick note: some noisy alerts from lower-priority routes — silencing to reduce pager fatigue: `pd-silence --match "route:analytics" --until +45m`
Mike: side-effect: noisy logs will balloon storage. I've set a TTL on the incident log bucket to 7 days to avoid retention blowout.
Tara: customer advisory posted to portal and emailed to enterprise contacts (AcmeCorp & BlueCart). Subject: "Intermittent telemetry delays affecting dashboards/traces — mitigation in progress"
Elaine: passing to next oncall at 02:00 UTC. handoff checklist in ticket. If anyone sees SLO breach evidence, escalate to P1 immediately.
Sam: handing off to Mike for overnight. I've documented what I flipped and why in RED-INC-2026-341.
Mike: ack, taking over. I'll keep the datadog liaison on the watch channel.
datadog-status-bot: UPDATE: "Service ingestion queues reduced — partial normalization. Some dashboards still delayed. Next update in 20 minutes."
Josh: Datadog shared a temporary agent config to reduce local sampling variance — applying to a small canary set first.
Nora: customer impact assessment (quick): - SLO risk: medium for billing write latency if traces stay missing >45m - Visible impact: dashboards for internal ops and enterprise customers; alerts rerouted to Prometheus successfully - User-facing errors: low evidence so far, but need verification from payment flows.
Tara: FYI CS already triaged priority tickets and linked them to this incident. We're offering a proactive note to top 10 paying customers.
Elaine: good work. record retrospective action: add cross-check in runbook to automatically failover alerts to Prometheus for any Datadog ingestion incident.
Sam: also recommend we automate local trace buffer toggle in our deploy pipeline (PR idea: infra#3421).
Mike: will monitor. if Datadog doesn't fully recover in 60m, we'll prepare to extend silences and keep customers updated.
Nora: last update for now: incident status = Mitigated (workarounds in place), monitoring recovery. moving to postmortem state once all data is backfilled.
Elaine: handoff complete — Mike owns overnight. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Mike: ack, I'll ping again on recovery or customer escalations.
